title: Representable diagonals descend along a locally covering open family
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] and size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets and let $(F_i\subseteq F)_{i\in I}$ be a small family of subsheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-pc-subfunctor]. Write $h_T(W)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(W,T)$ for schemes over $S$. Suppose each inclusion $F_i\to F$ is representable by open immersions [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-open-immersion]. Suppose each diagonal $F_i\to F_i\times F_i$ is representable, meaning that $h_T\times_{F_i}h_{T'}$ is represented by a scheme for every pair of schemes with maps to $F_i$. Assume the family fppf locally covers $F$: for every scheme $T$ and section $a\in F(T)$, there is an fppf covering $\{T_\alpha\to T\}$ and indices $i(\alpha)\in I$ for which $a|_{T_\alpha}$ belongs to $F_{i(\alpha)}(T_\alpha)$. Then for every $h_T\to F$, the open subschemes $V_i\subseteq T$ representing $h_T\times_FF_i$ cover $T$. For every pair $h_T\to F$, $h_{T'}\to F$, put $G=h_T\times_Fh_{T'}$ and $G_i=G\times_FF_i$. Each $G_i$ is represented by a scheme, and each inclusion $G_i\to G$ is representable by open immersions; on every scheme test of $G$ these opens cover that scheme. The functor $G$ is represented by a scheme over $S$. Consequently the diagonal $F\to F\times F$ is representable. No scheme atlas of any $F_i$ and no algebraicity hypothesis on a sheaf coproduct is required.

proof.text: Fix $a:h_T\to F$ and let $V_i\subseteq T$ represent $h_T\times_FF_i$. By [def-pc-open-subfunctor], a morphism $b:W\to T$ factors through $V_i$ precisely when $b^*a\in F_i(W)$. Choose the fppf covering $\{T_\alpha\to T\}$ and indices $i(\alpha)$ in the hypothesis. Every $T_\alpha\to T$ therefore factors through $V_{i(\alpha)}$. An fppf covering is jointly surjective by [def-pc-fppf-site]: for every point $t\in T$ choose a point above it in some $T_\alpha$; its image lies in $V_{i(\alpha)}$. Thus $T=\bigcup_i V_i$. The same argument applies to every scheme and every section of $F$, including $T'$ and its opens $V'_i$.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first and second paragraphs of proof

proof.text: For fixed maps $h_T\to F$ and $h_{T'}\to F$, write $a,b$ for their sections and define $G(W)=\{(u,v):u:W\to T,\ v:W\to T',\ u^*a=v^*b\}$. The subfunctor $G_i$ consists of such pairs whose common value lies in $F_i(W)$. The representing property of $V_i$ and $V'_i$ says exactly that $u$ and $v$ then factor uniquely through these two opens. The resulting sections in $F_i(W)$ agree: they have equal images in $F(W)$, and $F_i(W)\subseteq F(W)$ is an inclusion. Conversely, a pair of maps to $V_i,V'_i$ with equal images in $F_i(W)$ gives a pair in $G_i(W)$. These mutually inverse descriptions commute with every restriction $W_1\to W$, since they keep the two maps and their common value. Hence $G_i\cong h_{V_i}\times_{F_i}h_{V'_i}$. The assumed representability of the diagonal of $F_i$, in its stated pair-of-schemes form, gives a scheme representing this functor; this proves representability of every $G_i$.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first and second paragraphs of proof

proof.text: Let $h_W\to G$ be any scheme test, given by $(u,v)\in G(W)$, and put $c=u^*a=v^*b\in F(W)$. A morphism $r:Z\to W$ belongs to $h_W\times_G G_i$ precisely when $r^*c\in F_i(Z)$. By [def-pc-open-subfunctor] this is equivalent to factoring through the open $O_i\subseteq W$ representing $h_W\times_FF_i$ along $c$. Thus $h_W\times_GG_i\cong h_{O_i}$ over $h_W$, so $G_i\to G$ is representable by open immersions. Step 1 applied to $(W,c)$ gives $W=\bigcup_iO_i$; the universal section on each $O_i$ lies in $G_i(O_i)$. This proves the required covering property on every scheme test, not only on $T$ or on the representatives of the $G_i$.

source.place: Tag 02WR (lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces), first and second paragraphs of proof

proof.text: The Zariski topology on schemes over S is subcanonical (Mathlib Scheme.subcanonical_zariskiTopology and GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over), hence h_T and h_T' are Zariski sheaves. The fppf sheaf F is a Zariski sheaf by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf] and monotonicity of the sheaf condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The presheaf pullback G is a Zariski sheaf because limits of sheaves are sheaves (Sheaf.Limits.isSheaf_of_isLimit / ObjectProperty.prop_of_isLimit). This packages coordinatewise gluing and separatedness in the existing Mathlib limit theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] to $G$ on schemes over $S$ and its small family of subfunctors $(G_i)_{i\in I}$. Its four hypotheses have now been verified: the Zariski sheaf property is Step 4; representability of each $G_i$ is Step 2; representability of each inclusion by open immersions and the covering condition are Step 3. Consequently $G=h_T\times_Fh_{T'}$ is represented by a scheme over $S$. The index set is the original small $I$; the construction introduces no atlas of an $F_i$ and no sheaf coproduct.

source.place: Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), statement; applied in spaces.tex Tag 02WR, second paragraph

proof.text: Finally test $\Delta_F:F\to F\times F$ against any $h_W\to F\times F$, corresponding to $x,y\in F(W)$. By Step 5 choose a scheme $R$ representing $h_W\times_{x,F,y}h_W$. Its two projections give a scheme morphism $R\to W\times_SW$. Form $E=R\times_{W\times_SW}W$, where the second map is the scheme diagonal; both products exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $Z/S$, its universal property identifies maps $Z\to E$ with a single map $r:Z\to W$ such that $r^*x=r^*y$: the two maps to $W$ arising from $R$ must both equal $r$. This description is natural in $Z$ and is exactly $(h_W\times_{F\times F}F)(Z)$. Thus $E$ represents this diagonal test and $\Delta_F$ is representable as defined in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. In Lean this standard construction is supplied by Mathlib Functor.relativelyRepresentable.diag_of_map_from_obj: the representation of every pairwise pullback supplies its relatively representable maps, then the criterion gives the diagonal. Its existential witnesses are exactly those in def-trf-algebraic-space, with the trivial property.

lean.statement: theorem open_cover_representable_diagonal {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (I : Type u) (H : I → Subfunctor F.obj) (hH : ∀ i : I, Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (H i).toFunctor) (hopen : ∀ i : I, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (H i).ι) (hdiag : ∀ (i : I) (T T' : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (H i).toFunctor) (b : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (H i).toFunctor), (Limits.pullback a b).IsRepresentable) (hlocal : ∀ (T : Over S) (a : F.obj.obj (op T)), ∃ (𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left) (k : 𝒰.I₀ → I), ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, F.obj.map (Over.homMk (𝒰.f j) rfl : Over.mk (𝒰.f j ≫ T.hom) ⟶ T).op a ∈ (H (k j)).obj (op (Over.mk (𝒰.f j ≫ T.hom)))) : (∀ (T : Over S) (a : F.obj.obj (op T)) (V : I → T.left.Opens), (∀ (i : I) (W : Over S) (f : W ⟶ T), F.obj.map f.op a ∈ (H i).obj (op W) ↔ Set.range f.left ⊆ V i) → (⨆ i : I, V i) = ⊤) ∧ (∀ (T T' : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ F.obj) (b : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ F.obj), (∀ i : I, ((H i).preimage (Limits.pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).toFunctor.IsRepresentable) ∧ (∀ i : I, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) ((H i).preimage (Limits.pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).ι) ∧ (∀ (W : Over S) (c : (Limits.pullback a b).obj (op W)) (V : I → W.left.Opens), (∀ (i : I) (Z : Over S) (f : Z ⟶ W), (Limits.pullback a b).map f.op c ∈ ((H i).preimage (Limits.pullback.fst a b ≫ a)).obj (op Z) ↔ Set.range f.left ⊆ V i) → (⨆ i : I, V i) = ⊤) ∧ (Limits.pullback a b).IsRepresentable) ∧ IsRepresentable (prod.lift (𝟙 F.obj) (𝟙 F.obj))
